title: The forbidden reef: one night off North Sentinel
logline: A solo sailor's yacht drifts onto the reef of the world's most isolated island at night and must survive without going ashore.
essence: Surviving the forbidden reef means never stepping onto the beach.

hero.name: the sailor
hero.description: A solo sailor on a small yacht
hero.flaw: Alone, without power, and forbidden to go ashore.

hook.visual: The yacht heels on the reef at night; torches move on the beach behind the hero at the helm.

core_question.text: How do you survive the night without going ashore?

stakes.physical: A grounded hull on a falling tide.
stakes.legal_ethical: Contact with the island is forbidden.
stakes.mortal: The island's people turn every visitor back.

spine.once_upon_a_time: A solo sailor crosses the Andaman Sea.
spine.every_day: The yacht holds its course far from the island.
because_of_that: Because of that, the current drags the yacht to the reef.
Because of that, the sailor must wait aboard in the dark.
spine.until_finally: The beacon brings a patrol boat at dawn.
spine.ever_since: The sailor gives the island a wide berth.

narration.text: You are drifting onto the forbidden reef. In the dark.
The hull grinds on coral. Water slaps against the keel, louder every second.
On the beach, torches move. Someone is watching you.
But this is not where the story starts. It starts before dusk.
You had one rule out here. Never come near this island.
The hull grinds on coral. Water slaps against the keel, louder every second.
But the engine coughs once and stops. The silence is sudden and total.
You check the fuel. You check the battery. Nothing works.
The sea is calm around you, almost kind. That calm is the problem.
No lights. No power. Only the moon on the water.
You try the radio before panic sets in. Static answers you.
But the current has already taken hold of the yacht.

But the engine coughs once and stops. The silence is sudden and total.
You check the fuel. You check the battery. Nothing works.
The sea is calm around you, almost kind. That calm is the problem.
But the current does not drift. It pulls you toward the reef.
You brace at the rail and read the water. It is moving fast.
Sailors warned you about this stretch. They call it the wrong side.
Ahead, a dark line of trees rises out of the sea.
You know that shape from the charts. You were told never to go near it.
But there is no anchor that can hold you here.

Then the keel hits the reef. The whole boat lurches sideways.
You are thrown against the helm. Your hands find the wheel.
The hull holds. For now, the hull holds.
The tide is falling. Every minute, the coral rises around you.
You are stuck at the edge of an island nobody is allowed to visit.
But the reef is not the real danger tonight.

The hull holds. For now, the hull holds.
The tide is falling. Every minute, the coral rises around you.
But then you see the fires on the beach.
Shapes move between the trees. They are watching you.
The people here have lived alone for a very long time. They want it that way.
Every visitor before you was turned back. Some never left.
Your instinct says swim for help. That instinct is the mistake.
But staying aboard means waiting in the dark until dawn.

But you have one thing left. The emergency beacon in the cabin.
You pull the tab and raise it over your head. The light starts to pulse.
Now you wait. You do not shout. You do not wave at the beach.
You survive because you never set foot on that beach.
Then a patrol boat appears on the horizon, slow and careful.
